# Speed and rush

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Speed as a material: rushes into the cut, smears, streaks, thrown objects and decaying spin. 10 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Motion blur drawn as a few visible copies

`dv-tapped-blur-ghosts` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, sting

On the fastest frames the blur is not a smooth streak: a launching dot is two or three overlapping soft discs stacked along its path, a whipping sentence prints three or four offset copies of each word; speed reads as a graphic.

- **Build:** Recipe: render the moving layer four times at sub-frame offsets with opacity 1/4 each (the shutter with four samples and no extra blur). Anatomy: 3-4 taps at t - k dt / 4, each 25-35 % opacity, plus about 6 px of blur; dot taps 9-12 px apart, text taps about 18 px apart; only above about 12 px/f of travel. Sound: Whooshes on the whips.
- **Timing:** 6-12 f per move.
- **Use when:** Graphic, flat films; dots and type in flight.
- **Avoid when:** Photographic footage; films that use true shutter blur elsewhere.

### Things burst outward from the centre

`dv-burst-out` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, feature

Satellites fly out radially, growing to about 1.45x, and leave the frame while the label swaps on a kick; a square becomes a deck of about 30 source tiles that fans and bursts along a spiral and stops in 2 frames.

- **Build:** Build: burstOut(f, { at, n, from, to, grow: 1.45, spiral }) (fx/Orbit): radial positions on E.buildIn (26 f) with growth; spiral (degrees per index at full travel) fans a deck along a spiral; stop it on a HardStep. Anatomy: Radius 640 -> 925 px on an ease-in with growth; spiral burst then a hard stop. Sound: A label swap on the kick; a kick on the burst.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Orbit.burstOut`
- **Timing:** 26-28 f.
- **Use when:** Releasing a hub's contents; "from everywhere".
- **Avoid when:** Calm films.

### Two frames of streaks with stripe artefacts

`dv-streak-whip-frames` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, feature

Two frames of heavy horizontal streaking with vertical stripe artefacts (like a smeared barcode), then the next page arrives.

- **Build:** FlashCut's streak frame without the flash (streak only), held 2 f. Anatomy: The outgoing image stretched horizontally and cut into lines. Sound: A whoosh.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx`
- **Timing:** 4 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** A whip between two product pages.
- **Avoid when:** More than two frames.

### Rush: geometric acceleration into the cut

`dv-rush-ramp-cut` · transitions · signature · energy high · any

The rush: a line or a scroll drifts, then roughly doubles its speed every frame (2, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 18, 34, 88 px/f) and is hard-cut at the peak; the next shot opens at that speed and halves it every frame (259, 131, 54, 30, 18 px/f); a card can whip crisply (no blur) into the cut and be caught by a decelerating pan; shots can arrive smeared and settle their pan.

- **Build:** Build: <Rush cut dir vCut from out in lines lineColor> (fx/Rush): the outgoing layer builds on lib/handoff launch() (speed roughly doubling every 24 fps frame) and is cut on its fastest frame; the incoming one opens at the cut speed and halves it every 24 fps frame (carry()); copies draws 2-3 faint smear copies on the fastest frames, lines thin speed lines above 16 px/f; declares a velocity seam and camera blur above 100 px/f. Anatomy: Ratio x1.4-2.4 a frame on the way in; x0.5 a frame on the way out; crisp text up to about 52 px/f. Sound: A speech onset or a sub on the cut; a punchy hit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Rush`
- **Timing:** Exit 30-43 f; entry decay 30 f.
- **Use when:** Energy peaks; the hook of a launch; moving from one product moment to the next with force.
- **Avoid when:** More than two or three rushes per film; slowing before the cut.

### Tile wall whips in with per-tile parallax

`dv-tile-wall-whip` · ui choreography · accent · energy high · launch, feature

A wall of artwork tiles enters with heavy horizontal blur, each tile decelerating at its own rate (near tiles travel further), then the wall accelerates out and the next wall comes in.

- **Build:** parallax layers per tile row with whip in and out. Anatomy: Per-tile travel scaled by depth; blur on the fast frames. Sound: Whooshes.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** In 28 f, out 16 f cubic-in, next wall 52 f.
- **Use when:** Galleries of work; a portfolio beat.
- **Avoid when:** All tiles on one curve.

### Dragged paint as a pixel mosaic trailing the cursor

`dv-mosaic-paint-trail` · product demo · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A blob of the accent rendered in 15-20 px mosaic blocks trails behind the cursor like dragged paint, growing, its tail lagging about 10 frames, then retracting.

- **Build:** Recipe: the cursor path (closed form) sampled back in time, each sample stamping blocks of a grid. Anatomy: Trail sampled from the cursor path over the last 10 f, rasterised to a block grid. Sound: None needed. Materials: The trail is a row of stamped copies of one rounded blob along the path, each older stamp darker and less saturated, all drawn through a coarse pixelation (16 px blocks at 1080p, downscale then upscale nearest-neighbour) so soft edges show 3-4 brightness steps; it grows, cruises and shrinks with the cursor's speed and is sucked into the button.
- **Materials:** The trail is a row of stamped copies of one rounded blob along the path, each older stamp darker and less saturated, all drawn through a coarse pixelation (16 px blocks at 1080p, downscale then upscale nearest-neighbour) so soft edges show 3-4 brightness steps; it grows, cruises and shrinks with the cursor's speed and is sucked into the button.
- **Timing:** 44 f; retract 35 px/f.
- **Use when:** Drawing, painting, brushing tools.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth gradients for the trail (the mosaic is the look).

### Speed-gated motion blur

`tx-speed-gated-motion-blur` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy any · any

Fast whips, flings and flicked scrolls streak like a real shutter while holds and slow drifts stay pin-sharp, so the eye rests on the readable frames.

- **Build:** Never fake speed blur with CameraMotionBlur or an animated filter: blur() (they quantise to 8 bits and step); design the moves and let the master's render pass make the blur: `bash scripts/render.sh Film out/film.mp4 --blur` renders a 240-degree shutter centred on each frame, takes samples from measured speed (1 under 2 px/f, 4 up to 18 px/f, 14 at 60, 18 at 80) and averages them in float. Shape every fast move so its peak sits between 12 and 70 px/f (E.whip or E.inOut, or inertia() for a flicked scroll) and both ends fall under 2 px/f, so the streak exists only mid-move. Put every hard cut on an act boundary so samples never smear across it, and drive typed text, counters, carets and grain from fd(frame) so all sub-samples of a frame agree. Where optical flow cannot see the speed (a flat band wiping the whole frame) pass `--floor A-B:px` or analytic speed; in HyperFrames render at 4x fps and run `accumulate.py --uniform 4`, which is clean only to about 12-18 px/f. A crisp film renders only its fast frames with the shutter: declare them with blurRanges(shot, from, to, { film }) (lib/camera-moves.ts) for a camera move or fastRanges(speed, from, to) (lib/handoff.ts) for any speed (the frames over 720 px/s at 1080p, padded a frame each side) in CAMERA_BLUR or a primitive's declares(). Where the shutter pass is not wanted, draw the streak with DirBlur (fx/Defocus) from the layer's speed, as FlashCut and Wipe kind="push" do (smear 'draw'); never both on one layer.
- **Primitive:** `lib/defocus`, `lib/camera-moves.blurRanges`, `lib/handoff.fastRanges`, `fx/Defocus.DirBlur`
- **Timing:** Whip 12-20 f on E.whip with a 40-70 px/f peak, the shots either side at 0.3-1.5 px/f; streak length is about 2/3 of the per-frame travel (a 60 px/f card smears ~40 px); a flick is inertia(f, start, 50-70, 0.89), coasting ~8.6 x v0 px and under 0.5 px/f after its `settle` frames; nothing above 80 px/f. A move smears above 720 px/s at 1080p (24 px a frame at 30 fps, 12 at 60); a travelling hard edge carries a ramp 0.3 of its step.
- **Use when:** Any film with whips, flings, drops or flicked scrolls; walkthroughs that travel fast between setups and need every hold razor-sharp.
- **Avoid when:** Moves that would need more than 80 px/f (redesign as a cut on the beat, a match cut or a mask wipe); readable text moving above 20 px/f; a deliberately stepped on-twos section.

### Brushed micro-streaks

`tx-brushed-micro-streaks` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting

Fine directional streaks and a satin grain across a hero object's face make it read as machined material instead of flat vector.

- **Build:** Bake a brushed texture PNG offline at 2x the hero's on-screen size: seeded noise stretched along one axis (numpy noise, then a 1-D box blur 60-200 px long, normalised to sigma about 6 levels around mid-grey) so streaks are 1-2 px wide. Apply it as a child of the object inside its transform, masked to the face (`maskImage` of the face shape), blend overlay at opacity 0.06-0.10; a CSS `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,255,255,.04) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px)` is the quick version for a face that never scales down. As the object turns, slide the texture's backgroundPosition along the streak axis in proportion to its rotation so the satin seems to catch the light.
- **Timing:** Constant while the object is at hero scale (at least 30% of frame height); fade it out over 10-14 f on E.smooth before the object shrinks below that.
- **Use when:** Hero objects shown big enough for micro detail (coins, cards, devices, extruded marks); hardware and finance brands with a physical metaphor.
- **Avoid when:** Small or minified objects, where 1 px streaks alias and crawl; soft, friendly brands; flat UI.

### Graphic smear frames instead of motion blur

`dv-discrete-smear-frames` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · any

Speed is drawn as designed frames, not shutter blur: 2-3 faint offset copies trail a fast card for a few frames; the nearest figure has a 50 % double behind it; a label box stretches along a hop for exactly one frame; a line lunges 64 px and smears one frame before a scale snap; words are doubled or streaked on the first frame after a cut; a logo's first frame is a rotational blur ring.

- **Build:** Build: <Rush copies={{ n: 3, lag: 1, fade: 0.45 }}> (fx/Rush): 2-3 copies where the element was 1-3 frames ago, at 45 %, 20 %, 9 %, only on frames faster than 18 px/f, never across the cut; <Corners mode="jump"> draws the same idea as echo bars on markers. Anatomy: Copies at decreasing opacity along the motion; one-frame stretch; one-frame ghost. Sound: A kick on the logo cut; none for most.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Rush`
- **Timing:** 1-4 f.
- **Use when:** Stylised films where real blur would look soft; accents on single fast moments.
- **Avoid when:** Using it everywhere (it is an accent).

### Thin speed lines while velocity is high

`dv-speed-lines` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Three to five thin lines trail a fast object, converging toward it, visible only while it moves fast; comic speed dashes trail travelling items; a burst of short accent dashes streaks across horizontal bands while a title decodes; three parallel stripes shoot in at constant speed and stop dead at the hero.

- **Build:** Build: <Rush lines={{ n: 5 }} lineColor> (fx/Rush): thin bars along the travel whose strength follows the speed (from 16 to 40 px/f at 60 fps), seeded rows, never drawn below the threshold. Anatomy: 1 px lines 200-400 px long, opacity tied to speed; dashes 8-60 px; stripes 20 px stopping dead. Sound: A decode bed; the music drops out on the hard stop. Materials: After the stripes stop dead at the hero, 3-4 very faint thin lines continue past it to the frame edge (opacity 20 % -> 0 along their length), as if the motion had passed through and left a trace.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Rush`
- **Materials:** After the stripes stop dead at the hero, 3-4 very faint thin lines continue past it to the frame edge (opacity 20 % -> 0 along their length), as if the motion had passed through and left a trace.
- **Timing:** With the speed; bursts 42 f; stripes 12 f linear + a hard stop.
- **Use when:** A thrown object, a travelling message, a decode with energy.
- **Avoid when:** Lines on static frames.
